result.description: Google's online advertising platform; the Google Ads API lets developers programmatically manage accounts, campaigns, ads and pull reporting.
result.auth_detail: OAuth 2.0 (user consent flow) or service account workflow, both Google OAuth. Access levels are tied to the Google Cloud project that generated the OAuth credentials; developer tokens were reportedly sunset Sept 2026.
result.access_detail: Self-serve start: enabling the API gives Test access (test accounts only). Explorer access (2,880 ops/day on production) and Basic (15,000 ops/day, needs brand verification) need application review. Standard (unlimited) requires manual audit. Production use for third-party end users therefore needs Basic/Standard approval. Limits quoted from search summary and subagent report, not independently re-verified.
result.api_notes: Programmatic interface for managing large or complex accounts and campaigns: campaigns, ad groups, ads, budgets, bidding, assets, conversions, plus GAQL reporting. REST interface plus client libraries (Java, Python, etc.); gRPC is the historical primary transport but was not confirmed on the fetched page.
result.blocker: Production access beyond test accounts requires Google API access-level application (Explorer/Basic/Standard) with review and brand verification; Standard needs a manual audit. Docs on developer tokens vs Cloud-project-level access are in flux.

evidence.quote: Just like other Google APIs, Google Ads API uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol for authentication and authorization.
Your API access levels are determined by the Google Cloud project you used to generate your OAuth credentials.
After you've enabled Google Ads API, your Google Cloud project is granted Test access.
The Standard access application involves a detailed manual audit of your application.
Install a client library or call REST
The Google Ads MCP server provides a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API.
